title: Re-aim a laser tracker SMR in its magnetic drift nest at the tracker's new station, never lifting it
instruction: The tracker is now behind the beam post. Turn the SMR in its nest to face the post's pointer without lifting it or touching its optics, then let go.
context: Robot building: a new arm's base frame is located with a laser tracker from SMRs seated in drift nests on its base plate. When the tracker moves, each SMR is turned to face it (a cube corner accepts about 25 deg), never lifted off its land or touched on the optics: yaw by a pinch on the one line clear of the face, elevation by a fingertip roll.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y left, heights above the table. Base plate: painted blue-grey steel, 22 x 30 x 1.5 cm, centred x 27, y 0. Robot base: the base of a UR3e-size arm, no arm fitted: dark grey cast flange 12.8 cm across and 1 cm thick, a 9 cm round base joint housing 9 cm tall and a black 3 cm J1 cover, centred x 31, y +8 on the plate. Drift nest: Brunson 1.5THDN magnetic drift nest for 1.5 in SMRs, black anodized aluminium with a magnet under a 3-point land, 4.06 cm across, rim 1.27 cm above its foot, foot on the plate at x 24, y -6. SMR: 1.5 in (38.1 mm) red-ring SMR, polished 440C stainless steel ball, 150 g, open cube-corner face 22 mm across, seated in the nest, centre 2.86 cm above the plate (4.36 cm above the table); its face points left (+y) and 60 deg up. Beam post: grey steel rod 1.2 cm across on a 7 cm weighted foot at x 42, y -6, carrying in a yoke a pen laser pointer (1.6 cm across) whose red emitter sits 9.2 cm above the table and aims back at the ball centre (bearing straight ahead, 15 deg above the ball). Real trial: the SMR may be replaced by a 38.1 mm 440C steel ball with its face and rings painted on (see README).
scoring: Aim error A: angle between the SMR's face axis and the line from the ball centre to the pointer's emitter, mean of the last 1 s. Score 0 for the run if the ball is ever 3 mm or more off its land for 0.2 s, or a fingertip enters the open face (within 13 mm of the face axis, 12 to 30 mm out from the ball centre) 2 steps running. Otherwise 0 unless both grippers end 3 cm or more from the ball and the ball is still (yaw and tilt each under 0.5 deg change over the last 1 s). Then 1.0 if A <= 10 deg, 0.5 if A <= 20 deg, 0.25 if A <= 30 deg or the face's compass direction is within 10 deg of the bearing (yaw done), else 0. Start A is 77 deg; yaw alone leaves 45 (0.25), the roll alone 86 (0). Real trial: pointer spot on rings painted at 10, 20, 30 deg; lift: side cameras level with the ball top, a 3.0 mm cap on the seated ball marks the line, the top edge reaching it for 0.2 s scores 0.
reset_notes: Turn the ball back by hand (nitrile gloves, off the face) until the printed aim stem on the face lies along the 60 deg start wedge pointing left; seat it. Wipe pad marks with a lint-free cloth and alcohol; blow debris off the land.
fidelity: Approximate. Ball, nest (Brunson 1.5THDN, 40.6 mm), plate and post are real size. The seat is a lift slide plus yaw and tilt hinges about the ball centre. Brunson publishes no pull or seat torque: magnet = 3,000 N/m spring (9 N at 3 mm), friction 0.02 N m per hinge; the demo scored 1.0 in MuJoCo from half to double each and at 150-221 g. The ball collides as a full sphere; the cube corner is a black face, no optics. A pad within 3 cm of the ball at the end scores 0.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (raised both arms near their bases, never reached the ball or nest); demo: 1 (right arm pinched the ball in its nest, turned it, released and withdrew)
